definition: A machine learning approach where a model is trained on labeled input-output pairs so it can learn to predict outputs for new, unseen inputs.
A machine learning approach where a model finds hidden patterns or structures in unlabeled data without predefined output labels.
A machine learning paradigm where an agent learns to make decisions by taking actions in an environment and receiving reward or penalty signals based on outcomes.
A supervised learning task where the model predicts a continuous numeric output value, such as price, temperature, or revenue.
A supervised learning task where the model assigns each input to one of exactly two categories, such as spam vs. not-spam or fraud vs. legitimate.
A supervised learning task where the model assigns each input to one of three or more mutually exclusive categories.
A condition where a model learns the training data too well, including noise and outliers, causing poor generalization to new data. Indicated by high training accuracy but low validation accuracy.
A condition where a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the training data, resulting in poor performance on both training and validation sets.
The tension between a model's bias (error from oversimplification) and variance (error from oversensitivity to training data). Reducing one tends to increase the other.
The process of selecting, transforming, or creating input variables (features) from raw data to improve machine learning model performance.
A model evaluation technique that splits data into K equal folds, trains and evaluates the model K times each using a different fold as the validation set, then averages the results.
A classification metric that is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It balances both metrics and is especially useful when class distribution is imbalanced.

A condition in classification datasets where one class has significantly more samples than others, which can cause a model to be biased toward the majority class. Addressed via oversampling, undersampling, or class-weighted loss.
A problem where information from the test or future data inadvertently leaks into the training set, causing artificially high model performance that does not generalize to production.
The process of transforming numeric features to a common scale so that no single feature dominates model training due to magnitude differences.
A SageMaker feature for running inference on large datasets offline. It reads input from S3, runs the model, and writes predictions back to S3 without a persistent endpoint.
A neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms that processes sequential data in parallel rather than sequentially. It is the foundation for most modern large language models.

A deep learning architecture with two competing networks: a generator that creates synthetic data and a discriminator that tries to distinguish real from synthetic data. Used for image synthesis and data augmentation.

A neural network design where an encoder compresses input into a latent representation and a decoder reconstructs output from that representation. Used for translation, summarization, and image segmentation.
A generative model that learns a probabilistic latent space representation of data, enabling it to generate new samples by sampling from that space.
A compressed, lower-dimensional representation of data learned by a model. Points in the latent space encode the essential features of the input and can be decoded to generate new samples.
A language model that generates text one token at a time, conditioning each new token on all previously generated tokens. Used by models like GPT.
A latent diffusion model for generating high-quality images from text prompts by iteratively denoising a random latent representation guided by the text description.
A dense vector representation of a piece of data (text, image, or other) in a continuous vector space where semantically similar items are positioned closer together.
Embeddings that represent multiple data modalities (text, image, audio) in a shared vector space, enabling cross-modal similarity search and retrieval.
A large-scale AI model trained on broad datasets using self-supervised learning that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks through fine-tuning or prompting.
A phenomenon where a generative AI model produces outputs that are factually incorrect, fabricated, or inconsistent with the input, presented with apparent confidence.

A technique that grounds a language model's responses by retrieving relevant documents from a knowledge base at inference time, reducing hallucination and keeping responses current without retraining.
A fully managed AWS service that provides access to foundation models from Amazon and third-party providers via a single API, with tools for customization, RAG, and responsible AI.
A Bedrock feature that automates the RAG pipeline by managing document ingestion, chunking, embedding, and vector storage, making it easy to build retrieval-augmented applications.
A Bedrock feature that orchestrates multi-step tasks by enabling foundation models to plan and execute actions by calling APIs and external tools to complete complex user requests.
The date after which no new data was included when training a foundation model. The model has no knowledge of events or information published after this date.
The process of further training a pre-trained foundation model on a smaller, domain-specific dataset to adapt its behavior for a specific task or style.
A fine-tuning technique where human raters rank model outputs and the model is trained using reinforcement learning to produce responses humans prefer, improving alignment and helpfulness.
A prompting technique where the model is given a task description with no examples and expected to perform the task using its pre-trained knowledge.
A prompting technique that includes a small number of input-output examples in the prompt to guide the model's response format and reasoning style.
A prompting technique that encourages a model to reason step-by-step before producing a final answer, improving accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.
A prompting framework that interleaves reasoning steps with action steps, allowing a model to iteratively think and call external tools to solve complex tasks.
A prompting technique that generates multiple independent reasoning chains for the same question and selects the most frequently occurring answer, improving reliability on reasoning tasks.
A prompting technique that assigns the model a specific identity or role (e.g., 'You are an expert doctor') to shape the tone, style, and domain of its responses.
Specific strings provided in an inference request that signal the model to stop generating text when it produces them, useful for controlling output length and format.
A fine-tuning approach where a model is trained on diverse (instruction, response) pairs to make it better at following natural language instructions across a wide range of tasks.

Fine-tuning techniques that update only a small subset of model parameters (e.g., low-rank adapter matrices) rather than all weights, reducing compute and memory requirements while preserving model quality.
The process of adapting a model trained on general data to perform better on a specific domain by exposing it to domain-specific text through continued pre-training or fine-tuning.
A Bedrock option that reserves dedicated model capacity for a period of time, providing predictable throughput and lower per-token latency compared to on-demand usage.
A Bedrock feature that allows customers to import their own fine-tuned or trained model weights into Bedrock for managed inference without managing infrastructure.
A problem in neural network training where learning new tasks causes the model to lose performance on previously learned tasks, because new gradients overwrite old knowledge.
A capability that allows a language model to identify when to call external APIs or functions, generate structured call arguments, and incorporate the results into its response.

A mechanism in conversational AI applications that stores prior turns of a conversation (or a summary of them) and includes them in each prompt so the model maintains context across multiple exchanges.

A security attack where malicious content in an input causes an AI model to ignore original instructions and follow injected instructions instead, potentially exposing data or causing harmful outputs.
An AWS service that converts text to lifelike speech using deep learning, supporting many languages and voices. Used to build applications that talk or to add speech to content.
An AWS service that automatically extracts text, handwriting, and structured data (forms and tables) from scanned documents and images using machine learning.
An AWS service that provides image and video analysis using deep learning, including object detection, facial recognition, text detection, and content moderation.
A fully managed AWS service that provides real-time personalized recommendations using the same machine learning technology as Amazon.com, without requiring ML expertise.
An NLP service that extracts entities, key phrases, sentiment, syntax, and topics from text, and supports custom classification and entity recognition models.
A neural machine translation service that provides fast, high-quality, and affordable language translation between dozens of language pairs.
A fully managed service that uses machine learning to deliver highly accurate time-series forecasts, such as demand forecasting or resource planning.
A service for building conversational interfaces using voice and text, powered by the same deep learning technology as Alexa. Used to create chatbots and voice applications.
An enterprise search service powered by machine learning that indexes content from multiple data sources and returns precise, natural language answers rather than a list of links.
An NLP service that extracts medical information from unstructured clinical text, including conditions, medications, dosages, and medical entities, with HIPAA eligibility.
A fully managed service that uses machine learning to detect online fraud in real time, such as fake account creation or payment fraud, without requiring ML expertise.
A service that makes it easy to add human review to ML predictions, routing low-confidence predictions to a human workforce for validation before returning a final decision.
A SageMaker capability that continuously monitors deployed ML model endpoints for data quality drift, model quality degradation, bias drift, and feature attribution drift.
A centralized repository in SageMaker for cataloging, versioning, and managing ML models, with support for approval workflows and stage transitions from staging to production.
A CI/CD service for machine learning that allows teams to build, automate, and manage end-to-end ML workflows including data processing, training, evaluation, and deployment steps.
A SageMaker capability for organizing, tracking, and comparing ML training runs, including hyperparameters, metrics, and artifacts, to find the best performing model configuration.

A data labeling service that uses a combination of automated labeling and human review to create high-quality training datasets, including support for custom labeling workflows and inter-annotator agreement measurement.
An automated process for searching the hyperparameter space to find the configuration that maximizes model performance. SageMaker HPO supports Bayesian optimization and Hyperband strategies.
Algorithms for efficient similarity search in high-dimensional vector spaces. HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is commonly used in vector databases for fast retrieval in RAG systems.
A Bedrock feature for applying customizable safety and content policies to foundation model inputs and outputs, including topic blocking, sensitive information filtering, and grounding checks.
An Amazon-developed foundation model available through Bedrock that generates high-quality images from text prompts, with support for watermarking generated images for content provenance.
A model explainability technique that describes what input changes would cause the model to produce a different prediction, helping users understand why a decision was made and what could change it.
A model interpretability visualization that shows the marginal effect of one or two features on the model's predicted outcome while averaging out the effects of other features.
A post-hoc model explanation technique that explains individual predictions by fitting a simpler interpretable model locally around the prediction to approximate the complex model's behavior.
A set of metrics for evaluating automatic summarization and machine translation by comparing the overlap of n-grams between generated text and reference text.
A metric for evaluating machine translation quality by measuring the precision of n-gram matches between the generated translation and one or more reference translations.
A text evaluation metric that uses contextual embeddings from BERT to compute semantic similarity between generated and reference text, capturing meaning beyond exact word overlap.
A language model evaluation metric that measures how well the model predicts a text sample. Lower perplexity indicates better predictive performance on the held-out data.
A SageMaker tool that detects bias in training data and model predictions, and generates SHAP-based feature importance explanations to improve model transparency and fairness.
The property of a machine learning model that its predictions do not systematically disadvantage individuals or groups based on protected attributes such as race, gender, or age.

A mathematical framework for protecting individual privacy in datasets and model training by adding carefully calibrated noise so that the output cannot be used to infer information about specific individuals.
The presence of harmful, offensive, or abusive content in AI model outputs. Detected and filtered as part of responsible AI practices using content moderation classifiers or safety guardrails.
A technique for embedding an imperceptible signal in AI-generated content (text, images) to identify it as machine-generated, supporting content provenance and reducing misinformation.
Documentation artifacts in SageMaker that record a model's intended use, training data, evaluation results, and responsible AI considerations to support transparency and governance.
AWS-published documentation for each AI service that describes intended use cases, design choices, limitations, responsible AI considerations, and performance characteristics.
An international standard for AI management systems that provides requirements and guidance for organizations to demonstrate responsible AI governance, risk management, and continuous improvement.
A managed service for creating and controlling encryption keys used to protect data at rest and in transit across AWS services. Supports CMKs and AWS managed keys.
A service that records API calls and management actions across an AWS account, providing an audit trail for security analysis, compliance monitoring, and operational troubleshooting.
A portal that provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports, certifications, and agreements (such as SOC, PCI, ISO, and BAA) to support audit and regulatory requirements.
A service that continuously collects evidence of AWS resource configurations and usage to simplify audit preparation and help demonstrate compliance with frameworks like PCI DSS and HIPAA.
A data security service that uses machine learning to discover and protect sensitive data in S3, automatically identifying PII, financial records, and other sensitive content.
A service for securely storing, retrieving, and automatically rotating secrets such as database credentials, API keys, and OAuth tokens, with fine-grained IAM access control.

The documented history of data as it moves and transforms through a system, including its origin, how it was processed, and where it was used. Critical for compliance, debugging, and auditing ML pipelines.
A centralized, fully managed backup service that automates and consolidates backup tasks for AWS resources such as RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, EBS, and S3 across accounts and regions.
